subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx technical details & SLOs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.infer>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>, Aisha Khan <a.khan@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.infer>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: throughput sizing & SLOs (FinEx)

Hi Tom / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Call summary:
- Primary integration: customer-facing chat (interactive) + async summarization jobs.
- Key perf asks: interactive p95 latency target ~200ms (token streaming) and consistent throughput for peak windows.
- Preliminary workload: peak QPS estimated between 100-150 QPS, steady-state ~15-25 QPS.

What we need to size:
- Average tokens per response (including prompt + generated tokens) — you mentioned ~500 tokens on average but please confirm distribution (P50/P90/P99).
- Peak vs steady profile: hourly QPS (CSV) if available.
- Concurrency expectations (number of simultaneous open connections / chat sessions).
- Percent of requests requiring streaming vs full-response.

Action items:
1) Tom: share the hourly QPS/export and a sample of 50 typical payloads (anonymized).
2) Rafael: I’ve looped you in to draft a quick sizing note and outline options (dedicated vs hosted, batching profile, quantization suggestions).
3) We’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk through the CSV and sample payloads.

Notes / rough calc: if peak = 120 QPS and avg tokens/request = 600, that’s ~72k tokens/sec sustained at peak. Depending on model selection and quantization, that maps to multiple dedicated instances — we’ll provide a baseline in the sizing doc.

Attachments: none in this message (I’ll attach our initial template after Rafael adds his sizing).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.infer
[mobile redacted]

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.infer>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.infer>
Cc: Aisha Khan <a.khan@finex.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput sizing & SLOs (FinEx)

Neha —

Thanks for the recap. Attached is our export (hourly QPS for Mar 2026) and a short CSV with sample payload sizes. High-level clarifications below:

- Peak vs steady: our peak 1-hour window hits ~130 QPS (we see <2% of hours above that). Typical steady state during business hours is ~20-30 QPS. Night/maintenance windows are <5 QPS.
- Tokens per request: distribution from sample set: median 420, p90 780, p99 ~1400. Most UI interactions are ~400-600 tokens; heavy analysis prompts drive the high tail.
- Concurrency: in-chat websockets we expect ~35 concurrent sessions at peak (concurrency driven by number of users actively typing + long-running responses).
- Streaming: ~40% of interactive requests use streaming; batch summary jobs (async) are ~10% of total QPS but are bursty overnight.
- Latency targets: interactive client requires p95 <= 200ms for perceived realtime (we understand this is tight). For async jobs p95 <= 2s is acceptable.

We’ve attached: finex_traffic_2024_q1.csv (hourly QPS) and sample_payloads.csv (50 anonymized payload sizes).

Tom
Tom Ellis
Senior Eng Manager, Platform
FinEx Capital
[t.ellis@finex.com]

[Attachment: finex_traffic_2024_q1.csv (text/csv, 52KB)]
[Attachment: sample_payloads.csv (text/csv, 12KB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.infer>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.infer>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput sizing & SLOs (FinEx)

Thanks Tom — this is great data. I pulled the CSV and did a first-pass read: the peak/steady split and the token distribution help a lot.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll produce an initial sizing spreadsheet with two scenarios (hosted burstable and Dedicated reserved capacity) — will include GPU-count estimates, expected tokens/sec per instance, and a cost/latency tradeoff table.
- Needed from FinEx for a tighter estimate:
  * sample payload bodies (anonymized) for 10-15 of the p90/p99 cases so we can estimate generation token counts accurately, not just payload size.
  * confirmation of model family (are you planning to use a 13B/70B open model or a hosted LLM?) — that materially changes per-token throughput.
- Proposed tech deep-dive: Tue, Apr 6 at 10:00 PT — Rafael + Neha + Tom + Aisha + one infra engineer from our runtime team. We’ll walk the CSV and run through a quick sizing calc live.

Sizing note highlights (preview):
- Using conservative per-GPU throughput for a quantized 13B variant (~2k tokens/sec sustained) we’d need ~36 GPUs to cover 72k tokens/sec peak with headroom and concurrency; with a 70B optimized variant throughput per GPU drops so GPU count increases.
- With streaming, end-to-end client p95 is driven by both per-token latency and how quickly we can start sending tokens; we’ll outline batching/windowing strategies to keep p95 under 200ms for interactive flows where possible.

Attaching the initial template I’ll populate: redwood_initial_sizing.xlsx

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.infer

[Attachment: redwood_initial_sizing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)]
